title: POST /chat rejects a new conversation with no projectId before reaching the RAG backend
description: Without a projectId the AI service reads an empty project scope as org-wide and answers across every project in the organisation. The UI always sends one, so this 400 is the API contract enforcing the intent, not a UI-reachable path — verified here at the API layer.
preconditions: Valid JWT for an org member
steps: POST /api/assistant/chat with body { message: 'Show compliance status' } and no projectId anywhere (top-level or context.projectId)
expectedResult: Response is 400 Validation Error: 'A projectId is required to start a conversation. Select a project and try again.' No call is made to the Python RAG backend.

title: A follow-up message cannot override an existing conversation's stored projectId
description: Once a conversation exists, chat.routes.ts re-reads projectId from the stored conversation record (existing.projectId), not from the request body, before calling the RAG backend — closing a path where a client-supplied projectId on a follow-up could redirect retrieval to a different project than the one the thread was created in.
preconditions: An existing conversation created under Project A
Caller is a legitimate member of both Project A and Project B
steps: POST /api/assistant/chat with { conversationId: <projectA-conv>, message: 'follow up', projectId: <projectB-id> }
Inspect the org_context.project_id forwarded to the Python backend (via logs/mock)
expectedResult: The forwarded org_context.project_id is Project A's id (the conversation's stored value), never Project B's — the request-body projectId on a follow-up is silently ignored, not honoured.

title: assertProjectExistsInOrg rejects a stale/foreign projectId with a generic 403, without confirming which reason applies
description: ConversationService.assertProjectExistsInOrg queries `projects` with { _id, organizationId } from the caller's own JWT-derived org. A projectId that is either non-existent or belongs to another org both produce the same 'The selected project was not found in your organization' 403 — deliberately not distinguishing the two so the response cannot be used to fingerprint another tenant's project ids.
preconditions: Org B has a real project with a valid ObjectId
Caller is an org A user
steps: As an org A user, POST /api/assistant/conversations with { projectId: <org-B-real-project-id> }
Repeat with a syntactically valid but entirely made-up ObjectId
expectedResult: Both requests return the same 403 message ('...not found in your organization'), and neither leaks whether the id exists in another org versus not existing at all.

title: getConversation() rejects a conversationId belonging to a different user in the same org
description: T15a hardening: the Mongo filter requires ($or) userId match, missing userId (legacy), or null userId — a plain org-scoped filter would have let any org member read or extend any other member's conversation via a guessed/leaked ObjectId.
preconditions: User A and User B are both members of the same org
steps: As User B, call POST /api/assistant/chat with { conversationId: C_id, message: 'hi' }
expectedResult: Both requests return 404 Not Found for User B — conversation C's content and history are never returned to, or appended by, anyone but User A (or a legacy conversation with no userId set).

title: POST /chat/quick verifies project membership before forwarding to the RAG backend (MRB-03 regression guard)
description: Before the MRB-03 fix (2026-07-22), /chat/quick forwarded whatever projectId the client sent straight to the Python RAG backend with no membership check, letting a user fish another project's indexed data through the stateless quick-chat path even though the conversational /chat path was already hardened. assertProjectAccess must now be called first.
preconditions: Caller belongs to Project A only
Project B exists in the same organization
steps: POST /api/assistant/chat/quick with { message: 'summarize this project', projectId: <Project B id> }
expectedResult: Request is rejected with 403 ProjectAccessDeniedError before any call reaches the Python backend — no data from Project B's indexed corpus is returned.

title: Per-user rate limit on /chat returns 429 with a human-readable retry message after 10 requests/minute
description: Each of /chat, /chat/stream and /chat/quick carries a route-level rateLimit config keyed by userId||sub||ip, max 10 per 1-minute window, with a custom errorResponseBuilder — distinct from and tighter than the plugin-level global/per-user/per-org limits in rate-limit.ts.
preconditions: Valid JWT for a single test user
steps: Send 10 POST /api/assistant/chat requests in rapid succession as the same authenticated user
Send an 11th request within the same 60-second window
expectedResult: The 11th request returns 429 with body { success:false, error:'Too Many Requests', message:'AI assistant rate limit exceeded. Try again in N seconds.', statusCode:429 }.

title: chat() retries a transient Python backend failure up to 3 times with exponential backoff before surfacing an error
description: executeWithRetry() retries RETRY_COUNT (default 3) times with delay RETRY_DELAY_MS * 2^(attempt-1) (1s, 2s, 4s) only when isRetryableError() is true; a non-retryable error or the final attempt propagates immediately.
preconditions: Python AI backend mocked to fail with ECONNRESET on the first 2 calls, then succeed on the 3rd
steps: Invoke pythonBackendClient.chat(request) against the mocked backend
Observe the number of attempts and inter-attempt delays
expectedResult: The call succeeds on the 3rd attempt; delays between attempts are approximately 1000ms then 2000ms; the final ChatResponse is returned to the caller with no error surfaced.

title: GET /conversations/:id/messages returns metadata.blocks so a reloaded conversation still renders tables
description: Assistant answers are persisted as prose only (toStoredNarrative strips tables); the rendered tables/stat-tiles/donuts live exclusively in message.metadata.blocks. The route's response schema must declare metadata as an object with additionalProperties:true, or Fastify's strict serialisation silently drops it and reopening a past conversation shows narrative with the data gone.
preconditions: A prior conversation exists whose latest assistant message rendered a table block
steps: Send a chat message that produces a table block (e.g. 'list evidence items')
Reload the page / call GET /api/assistant/conversations/:id/messages fresh
Inspect the returned assistant message's metadata field
expectedResult: metadata.blocks in the response contains the original table block data (columns/rows), so the client can re-render the table identically to the live turn, not just the stripped narrative.
